papers.title: TACO: An open, interpretable model for microsecond-scale TCR specificity prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting antigen-induced T-cell activation from T-cell receptor (TCR) and peptide sequence remains difficult for TCRs and peptides not represented in training data. We present TACO (T-Cell Activation from Chemistry and Orientation), an open statistical model for predicting TCR specificity against HLA-A*02:01-presented peptides. TACO takes as input the peptide sequence and six TCR CDR loop sequences. Learning from binary activation labels, TACO selects a single canonical orientation of the CDR loops over the peptide and learns five amino-acid contact-potential matrices as well as two peptide-exposure profiles.The orientation is fixed and does not require experimentally determined or predicted structures. We evaluate TACO on held-out peptides separated by Levenshtein distance at least four from all training and validation peptides, limiting near-neighbor shortcut learning. TACO achieves AUROC 0.67 on a large held-out activation dataset and 0.68 on IMMREP25 HLA-A*02:01, exceeding the open structure-based models evaluated here and matching the reported AlphaFold3-TCRdock result. The model has 2,019 fitted parameters, retains most within-peptide ranking signal with TCR$beta$ sequence alone, and reaches 406,000 TCR--peptide predictions per second on CPU. This throughput enables computational evaluation of large TCR-peptide search spaces. We show its potential use for prioritizing candidate target peptides from large peptide libraries, reducing the search space for downstream experimental investigation. TACO fitted parameters also expose candidate physicochemical patterns that can be inspected directly. We release TACO's parameters and complete training, evaluation, and inference code.

papers.title: TGF-b/TIF1g signaling restrains CD8+ T cell expansion while preserving cytotoxic competence
papers.abstract: Transforming growth factor b exerts complex and often opposing effects on CD8+ T cell biology, yet the molecular mechanisms that distinguish these functions remain poorly understood. Here, we identify TIF1g (TRIM33) as a critical signal threshold regulator that couples TGF b signaling to CD8+ T cell activation and cytotoxic function. In the presence of TGF b, TIF1g deficient CD8+ T cells bypass canonical suppressive signals and acquire a transcriptional program characterized by enhanced activation and proliferation. Despite this hyperactivated state, TIF1g deficient cells fail to acquire full effector function, exhibiting markedly reduced Granzyme B and Perforin expression under TGF b signaling. We confirmed this functional uncoupling in vivo using a secondary Listeria monocytogenes challenge model, in which TIF1g deficient CD8+ T cells underwent robust expansion yet failed to efficiently control bacterial infection because of impaired cytotoxic activity. In a lymphopenic homeostatic proliferation model, TIF1g deficiency disrupted cellular quiescence, leading to excessive proliferation and spontaneous effector differentiation. Consistent with these findings, loss of TIF1g accelerated B16 melanoma growth and was associated with reduced Perforin expression in tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells. Together, these findings identify TIF1g as a key regulator of TGF b mediated CD8+ T cell responses, uncoupling activation from cytotoxic differentiation and revealing a mechanism by which TGF b independently regulates proliferative and effector programs.

papers.title: Monounsaturated fatty acid depletion is a metabolic pattern of pathogenesis surveilled to activate p38 MAPK innate immunity
papers.abstract: Pathogen infection profoundly remodels host metabolism. Whether hosts sense specific pathogen-induced metabolic changes to identify microbial infection is not known. Here, we find that depletion the monounsaturated fatty acid oleate is a metabolic pattern of pathogenesis, specifically surveilled by the nematode C. elegans to identify active infection with a bacterial pathogen. We previously demonstrated that the enzymatic TIR (Toll/interleukin-1 receptor/resistance)-domain containing protein, TIR-1/SARM1, the key upstream activator of p38 MAPK PMK-1 immunity, is a guard protein in an effector-triggered immune response, positioned specifically on the surface of lysosome-related organelles to sense the toxic effects of bacterial infection. Here, we show that acute loss of oleate in intestinal cells during bacterial infection causes lysosome-related organelles to collapse, which induces the aggregation and activation of TIR-1/SARM1. Further, we find that oleate deficiency is a host vulnerability that concomitantly activates the c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) KGB-1 nutrient sensing pathway, an adaptive response that promotes expression of TIR-1/SARM1 on lysosome-related organelles and is required for survival during infection. These data establish a mechanistic connection between fatty acid nutrition and innate immune regulation, and reveal that specific changes in host metabolism are surveilled to identify pathogen attack.

papers.title: A mammalian fibroblast zoo reveals barriers to cross-species virus replication and differential regulation of antiviral immunity
papers.abstract: Virus zoonosis represents a continual threat to humans. Viruses emerge in humans directly or indirectly through interactions with mammals. However, our understanding of virus-host susceptibility across the diversity of mammals is limited and experimental model systems are restricted to a very small set of model organisms. Mammals are highly diverse and different habitats, lifestyles, diets, and exposures to different pathogens have driven substantial genetic diversity. We generated a library of primary fibroblasts across 86 mammalian species and used these cells to build an atlas of virus-host susceptibility across a panel of arboviruses that infect diverse mammals including humans. Perturbing the innate immune system revealed some virus-host pairs where restriction is controlled by the immune system and others where there is an incompatibility with host factors. Transcriptomic profiling of the library in response to virus sensing mimicked by poly(I:C) or antiviral signaling with type I interferon reveals a core set of conserved genes that respond as well as substantial species- and order-specific responses. Together these data provide a comparative atlas of innate immune responses across mammals and offer a window into how these systems have evolved across animals.

papers.title: A reporter mouse model to map RIG-I expression and function in vivo
papers.abstract: The cytosolic RNA sensor RIG-I is a critical component of the innate immune response to RNA viruses, yet few tools exist to track RIG-I in vivo. Herein, we report the development of a RIG-I reporter mouse, termed RIG-ImScar, that enables fluorescence imaging and tractable immunoprecipitation of RIG-I in vivo. These mice revealed enrichment of RIG-I expression in circulatory, lymphoid, and mucosal tissues and broad expression across immune cell types. RIG-I itself is upregulated in response to IFN. To distinguish RIG-I sentinel cells, which are programmed to express RIG-I at steady state, from IFN-responder cells, we crossed RIG-ImScar mice with Mx1GFP mice. Blocking IFNAR with a monoclonal antibody showed that basal RIG-I expression in immune cells was largely independent of type I IFN signaling, although Ly6Chi monocytes required IFNAR for RIG-I expression. To probe functional responses in vivo, we intranasally administered a RIG-I-specific agonist, SLR14. Mapping RIG-I expression across the lung identified alveolar macrophages as a critical RIG-I sensor cell population, and depletion of alveolar macrophages, but not neutrophils, slightly impaired lung IFN responses. Together, these findings support the use of the RIG-ImScar model to probe RIG-I dynamics in vivo and predict functional sensor cell populations across tissues.

papers.title: γδ T cell-derived IL-17A aggravates experimental epidermolysis bullosa acquisita in response to IL-1β
papers.abstract: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita (EBA) is a mucocutaneous autoimmune blistering disorder mediated by autoantibodies against type VII collagen and subsequent splitting of the dermal-epidermal junction. Interleukin (IL)-17A promotes the production of chemokines and cytokines involved in neutrophil recruitment and activation, suggesting that IL-17A may contribute to EBA pathogenesis. We aimed to clarify the role of IL-17A in experimental EBA. Using an antibody transfer-induced EBA mouse model, we demonstrate that IL-17A promotes disease development, as pharmacological blockade of IL-17A with a neutralizing antibody ameliorated skin lesions. Gamma-delta ({gamma}{delta}) T cells were identified as the predominant cellular source of IL-17A, supported by the attenuated disease phenotype observed in {gamma}{delta}TCR-deficient mice. In addition, CD4+ T cells and neutrophils contributed to IL-17A production in experimental EBA. Mechanistically, IL-1-beta, rather than IL-23, was identified as a critical mediator of IL-17A production by {gamma}{delta} T cells in vitro, consistent with our in vivo findings. Whereas EBA severity was not reduced in IL-23p19-deficient mice, disease was markedly attenuated in IL-1R-deficient animals. Together, our study provides the first evidence that {gamma}{delta} T cell-derived IL-17A plays a pivotal role in experimental EBA and identifies a previously unrecognized IL-1{beta}/{gamma}{delta} T cell/IL-17A axis that expands current understanding of EBA immunopathogenesis.

papers.title: HIV-1 Vpu complements HLA-A downregulation by Nef and impairs TCR-mediated recognition of HIV-infected cells through distinct mechanisms
papers.abstract: Many viruses, including HIV-1, target the human leukocyte antigen (HLA) class I molecules HLA-A, HLA-B, and HLA-C to evade immune surveillance. HIV-1 Nef selectively downregulates HLA-A and HLA-B, whereas Vpu variants from primary strains reduce cell-surface HLA-C expression. Whether HIV-1 also uses Vpu to target other HLA molecules has remained unclear. Here, we show that Vpu from primary strains reduces HLA-A, including the globally prevalent HLA-A2, on infected cells. Although Nef is the principal modulator of these molecules, Vpu acts independently of Nef and impairs TCR-mediated recognition of infected cells in co-culture systems. However, the reduction in TCR signaling is also dependent on the presence of BST2/tetherin, a restriction factor that retains nascent virions and targets them for degradation. HLA-A2-restricted, HIV-specific CTL responses were lowest when both Nef and Vpu were present. Vpu variants from chronic and transmitted/founder strains, but not from the prototypical recombinant strain NL4.3, were sufficient to reduce cell-surface HLA-A2, although activity varied widely among variants and appears to have arisen independently in different hosts. Coimmunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence analyses showed that Vpu interacts with HLA-A2 and redirects it to a perinuclear compartment which is probably the trans-Golgi network through a mechanism governed by the Vpu N-terminus/transmembrane domain. Overall, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized function of Vpu and show how HIV-1 uses Nef and Vpu to limit HLA-A-mediated viral antigen presentation and promote immune evasion.

papers.title: Title: Combinatorial bnAb and T Cell Immunization Enhances Post-Infection Control of SHIVSF162p3 Viremia in Rhesus Macaques
papers.abstract: An ideal HIV-1 vaccine should provide broad protection against most HIV-1 variants, control early dissemination of infected cells after virus acquisition, and avoid the risk that vaccine-induced, HIV-specific CD4+ T cells serve as targets for viral transmission. In this study, we modeled this complex host-virus interaction in rhesus macaques challenged with a single high dose of SHIVSF162p3. Specifically, we evaluated the impact of T cell immunization with a human adenovirus-5-based candidate vaccine encoding an SIV Gag-Tat fusion (AdHu5SIVGag/Tat) alongside a partially protective, limiting dose of the broadly neutralizing antibody (bnAb) PGT121. Immunization with AdHu5SIVGag/Tat elicited Gag-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cell responses in PBMC and mucosal tissue. T cell vaccination did not affect PGT121-mediated protection against SHIVSF162p3 acquisition. However, independently of vaccination, constitutively activated CD4+4{beta}7+Ki-67+ T cells in rectal tissue attenuated PGT121-mediated protection. Crucially, a unique pattern of post-infection control of SHIVSF162p3 viremia emerged in AdHu5SIVGag/Tat-immunized, PGT121-treated animals, characterized by an increased eclipse phase, lower peak viremia, and a late-phase decay in steady-state viremia. These results suggest potential synergy between bnAbs and AdHu5SIVGag/Tat-induced antiviral T cell responses, with significant implications for HIV-1 vaccine development and early interventions following infection.

papers.title: Live attenuated YFV-17D vaccine induces robust B and T cell immunity in vaccine-draining lymph nodes
papers.abstract: The yellow fever virus-17D (YFV-17D) vaccine is widely regarded as one of the most effective vaccines in existence, with protection linked to robust elicitation of neutralising antibodies1. The features of the germinal centre (GC) reaction driving this durable and potent antibody responses remain unclear. Here we examined immune dynamics in blood and lymph nodes (LNs) after primary YFV-17D immunisation in humans. Using fine needle biopsy (FNB), we identified robust T and B lymphocyte responses within draining LNs, underpinning maturation of antibodies targeting the viral envelope (E). Early antibody responses were largely IgM, with gradual accumulation of E-specific memory B cells and anti-viral IgG in the subsequent months. Monoclonal antibodies derived from GC B cells had specificity for E, with diversification in the LN capable of driving increases in binding and neutralising potency. While circulating vaccine-specific CD4+ T cells peaked two weeks post-vaccination, clonally related GC and IL-10+ T follicular helper populations progressively accumulated in the LN. Comparison of FNB transcriptional datasets following YFV-17D, SARS-CoV-2 mRNA/LNP, and seasonal influenza vaccination identified a conserved GC program involving similar B and T lymphocyte subpopulations. Collectively, we find that while YFV-17D induces robust GC activity, this trait is shared with other vaccine platforms and the notably durable protection against infection may reflect an incapacity of the virus to escape host immunity.

papers.title: Robust T and B cell activation is associated with rapid clearance of infectious SARS-CoV-2
papers.abstract: The immunologic correlates of rapid clearance of SARS-CoV-2 shedding are not well understood, partly due to challenges of collecting samples early after infection and the fact that most studies do not measure infectious virus. Here, we performed mass cytometry profiling of peripheral blood cells collected from people 4-6 days after onset of symptoms from acute SARS-CoV-2 infection who underwent daily nasopharyngeal testing for SARS-CoV-2 culture positivity. We identified broad and coordinated activation of innate and adaptive immune cells in unvaccinated individuals with primary infection. Faster clearance of infectious virus shedding was associated with robust adaptive immune cell activation and proliferation, namely among cytotoxic CD8+, CD4+, and {gamma}{delta} T cells and plasmablasts. In contrast, vaccinated individuals who rapidly cleared breakthrough infection showed minimal cellular immune activation. Our findings identify early immune correlates of rapid clearance of infectious SARS-CoV-2 shedding that may inform future prevention and therapeutic approaches to reduce disease burden and transmission.

papers.title: Clonally Convergent Tph/Tfh-like CD4+ T Cells are Shared Across Recovery and Recurrence in Experimental Periodontitis
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease of the tooth-supporting structures (periodontium) that requires life-long maintenance to prevent progression. Using a sensitized model of recurrent periodontitis in mice (SeRPD), in which regulatory breakdown was induced by temporary Treg depletion concurrent with disease, we mapped the gingival T cell imprint across each disease phase. Transient regulatory breakdown left a durable mucosal imprint after clinical recovery, characterized by enrichment of local and regional CD4 T cells. Paired single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing of gingival immune cells identified a convergent clonotype expanded from recovery into recurrence that carried a Tfh/Tph-like transcriptional identity. An analogous CD4 T cell population was detected in human periodontitis lesions by single-cell transcriptomics. Together, these findings support a paradigm in which clinical recovery does not ensure a local T cell repertoire reset; instead, a reservoir of antigen-experienced, tissue-adapted CD4 T cells persist in the mucosa and participate in recurrence.

papers.title: A fibroblast-CD8+ T cell circuit drives a Type 1 shift in allergic inflammatory memory
papers.abstract: Inflammatory memory in barrier tissues often manifests as exaggerated recall responses to previously encountered stimuli. While recall is generally thought to reinforce the Type of inflammation (e.g., Type 1 (T1), Type 2 (T2), or Type 17 (T17)) induced in the primary encounter, whether and how memory responses engage programs beyond the initiating Type is unclear. Here, we adapted well-characterized murine models of T2 atopic dermatitis (AD)-like and T17 psoriasis-like inflammation into repeated challenge paradigms to compare how inflammatory memory is stored and recalled through longitudinal single-cell RNA-sequencing. In T17 inflammation, a network of IL-17-producing {gamma}{delta}T cells, IL-17-responsive keratinocytes and myeloid cells established in primary challenge re-emerged in recall with increased abundance and accelerated kinetics. By contrast, allergic T2 memory drove a particularly exacerbated and durable recall response in which hallmark features of T1 immunity, including interferon (IFN) signaling and cytotoxic lymphocyte recruitment, were unexpectedly layered onto amplified T2 responses. This T2-to-T1 shift was initiated by CD8+ tissue-resident memory T (Trm) cells that expanded with repeated challenge, produced IFN{gamma}, TNF- and IL-13, and closely resembled treatment-refractory Trm cells in AD. Tissue rewiring was supported by Trm-derived T1 cytokines and the IL-4-rich T2 milieu whose synergy on fibroblasts amplified allergic recall via IL-15 and CCL19. By tuning fibroblast IFN responsiveness in vivo, we mechanistically dissect how this fibroblast-CD8+ T cell circuit supports cytotoxic CD8+ T cell responses. In human AD, both arms of allergic recall amplification by this two-cell circuit featuring T1 and T2 effector responses were conserved. Our findings reveal how a stromal-immune circuit drives a clinically relevant T1 immune axis to support allergic inflammatory memory.

papers.title: High-fat diet promotes exhaustion-associated T-cell remodeling across vascular and lymphoid tissues in atherosclerosis-prone mice
papers.abstract: Background: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease driven by lipid accumulation and immune dysregulation. How chronic dietary lipid exposure reshapes T-cell states across vascular and lymphoid tissues, and whether these changes resolve after dietary normalization, remains incompletely defined. This study examined diet-associated T-cell remodeling and the contribution of macrophage-mediated stimulation. Methods: ApoE-deficient mice received a vegetarian diet (VD) or high-fat diet (HFD) for 12 or 24 weeks; a dietary reversal group received HFD for 12 weeks followed by VD for 12 weeks. CD45-positive cells from aorta, blood, spleen, lymph nodes, and bone marrow underwent single-cell RNA sequencing with matched T-cell receptor sequencing. T cell states were annotated using canonical markers, and exhaustion- and naive-associated programs were quantified using UCell scores. Analysis assessed T-cell composition, clonal expansion, and predicted macrophage-T cell communication, with splenic flow-cytometric validation. Results: HFD was associated with enrichment of exhaustion-associated states, with the highest exhaustion scores in the aorta. At 24 weeks, the pooled exhausted-cell proportion was 15.7% under HFD versus 10.6% under VD. Dietary reversal restored this proportion to 10.6%, while residual transcriptional changes persisted in a tissue-dependent manner. Flow cytometry corroborated increased inhibitory receptor expression and co-expression. Aortic macrophages exhibited inflammatory and antigen-presentation programs alongside increased predicted communication with T cells. Aortic T-cell activation and clonal expansion accompanied these changes, and clonotype size correlated with exhaustion score (Spearman correlation coefficient = 0.57, p = 0.029). Conclusion: Chronic HFD is associated with multicompartment T-cell remodeling, with prominent vascular exhaustion-associated programs and tissue-dependent recovery after dietary normalization. These findings suggest that dietary lipid exposure may leave a durable adaptive immune imprint across organs during atherosclerosis.

papers.title: Can the Human Plastisphere Account for the Rise of Type 1 Diabetes: A Computational Molecular Mimicry Study
papers.abstract: An increased incidence of childhood type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) has been widely documented, but its pathophysiological origins are poorly understood. The post-World War II expansion of the plastics industry in the United States and elsewhere coincides with a marked increase in T1DM incidence; however, no pathophysiological mechanism has been proposed that could justify such a temporal correlation. Here, we leverage recent advances in artificial intelligence and protein structure prediction and binding to show that molecular mimicry is a plausible pathophysiological mechanism for plastic fragments to induce onset of T1DM for individuals with certain HLA haplotypes.

papers.title: Structural and evolutionary insights into FcαμR recognition of polymeric immunoglobulins
papers.abstract: Polymeric immunoglobulins (pIgs) are central to adaptive immunity in jawed vertebrates. FcR is a bispecific pIg receptor that recognizes both IgM and IgA, but the molecular basis has been unclear. Here we determine cryo-EM structures of mammalian FcR bound to IgM or IgA and show that FcR engages each ligand in a 1:1 stoichiometry, with higher affinity for IgM. The FcR-binding site overlaps with those of pIgR, and also with the preferred FcR-binding site on IgM, yet distinct features distinguish FcR from both pIgR and FcR. Functionally, FcR efficiently internalizes both IgM and IgA through a pathway independent of the di-leucine motif. Structures of amphibian pIgR and FcR bound to IgM further shed light on the evolutionary diversification of the FcR/pIgR family. Together, these findings define the structural basis of FcR-mediated pIg recognition and provide a framework for understanding the evolution of pIg receptors.

papers.title: MULTI-COHORT TRANSCRIPTOMIC ANALYSIS REVEALS SHARED INFLAMMATORY SIGNALING AND UROTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION ACROSS IC/BPS PHENOTYPES
papers.abstract: Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) is a heterogeneous disorder characterized by bladder pain, inflammation, and urothelial dysfunction, yet the molecular features shared across clinically defined disease phenotypes remain incompletely understood. Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and acyloxyacyl hydrolase (AOAH), a regulator of TLR4 ligand activity, have been implicated in IC/BPS in clinical and preclinical mechanistic studies. Here, we performed a multi-cohort reanalysis of four independent human IC/BPS transcriptomic datasets spanning bladder tissue and urine sediment from non-ulcer/non-Hunner, ulcerative/Hunner, normal-capacity, low-capacity, non-lesion, and lesion phenotypes. We evaluated immune cell-associated expression, urothelial differentiation and barrier integrity, TLR4 and pro-inflammatory signaling, and AOAH expression. IC/BPS exhibited phenotype-specific immune remodeling, yet shared features were also identified. Bladder-tissue IC/BPS was consistently associated with reduced expression of urothelial differentiation and barrier markers, together with increased TLR4 recognition and pro-inflammatory signaling. AOAH expression was elevated across all three bladder-tissue cohorts and was associated with monocyte/macrophage and pro-inflammatory transcriptional states. TLR4 signaling similarly paralleled myeloid and inflammatory features, whereas inflammatory programs generally showed inverse relationships with urothelial barrier markers. Notably, independently defined severe phenotypes of ulcerative IC and low-capacity IC showed concordant molecular remodeling characterized by increased leukocyte and monocyte/macrophage signatures, enhanced TLR4 signaling, elevated AOAH expression, and reduced urothelial barrier-associated expression. Together, these findings identify reproducible molecular signatures that extend across IC/BPS phenotypes and support a model in which urothelial dysfunction and TLR4-AOAH-associated myeloid inflammatory states coexist across disease phenotypes. These results provide a molecular framework for stratifying IC/BPS beyond clinical labels and identify shared and subtype-specific molecular signatures that may inform therapeutic response evaluation and clinical management.

papers.title: PIM6 Induces Tolerance and Confers Protection against Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Primary Macrophages
papers.abstract: Glycolipids are major components of the mycobacterial cell envelope and play critical roles in host-pathogen interactions. Here we investigate the capacity of the mycobacterial glycolipid phosphatidyl-myo-inositol hexamannosides (PIM6) to modulate innate responsiveness in naive primary human monocytes and monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs). Monocytes and MDMs prestimulated with PIM6, followed by 5 days of rest, secreted attenuated levels of tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF-), interleukin 6 (IL-6), and interleukin 10 (IL-10) following LPS challenge. PIM6 pretreatment significantly altered pattern recognition receptor expression through the experimental time course and programmed a tolerized phenotype in myeloid cells independent of TLR2 activity. In an infection challenge with H37Rv Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M.tb), MDMs pretreated with PIM6 secreted decreased levels of TNF- and IL-10 and exhibited early increased bacterial control. Together, these data reveal PIM6 as a complex immunomodulator that tolerizes myeloid cells to subsequent stimuli and exerts direct effects on the control of M.tb infection.

papers.title: CD200R1 Marks a Branchpoint During Human Natural Killer Cell Development in Tonsils
papers.abstract: Human natural killer (NK) cells arise from common innate lymphoid cell (ILC) progenitor and precursor populations that are selectively enriched within secondary lymphoid tissues (SLTs) and that complete their terminal differentiation through stages of progressively lineage-restricted downstream developmental intermediates. We identify two subsets of tonsil CD94/NKG2A+NKp80- (stage 4A) NK-cell development intermediates that show differential expression of the inhibitory receptor, CD200R1. Ex vivo single-cell transcriptomic, DNA methylation, phenotypic, and functional analyses demonstrate that CD200R1 stage 4A cells represent an immature, oligopotent precursor population enriched for tissue-resident and cytokine-responsive programs. In contrast, CD200R1- stage 4A cells show more restricted NK-cell developmental potential concomitant with features of mature NK cells. These findings help to refine the human NK cell developmental pathway in tonsils and highlight CD200R1 as a useful marker delineating an uncommitted developmental state linking microenvironmental cues to NK-cell maturation and plasticity.

papers.title: MHCII+ cancer-associated fibroblasts promote antitumor immunity in pancreatic cancer
papers.abstract: The functions of major histocompatibility complex class II molecule-expressing cancer-associated fibroblasts (MHCII+CAFs) in pancreatic cancer remain controversial. MHCII+CAFs are primarily described as immunosuppressive, as MHCII allows for direct interaction with, and support of, regulatory T cells (Tregs). However, MHCII+CAF functions may be more complex depending on their origins and their cellular interactions within the tumor microenvironment. Here, using orthotopic models of pancreatic cancer, we show that conventional CD4+ T cells and their production of Interferon gamma (IFN{gamma}) increased MHCII+CAFs in tumors. Acute depletion of Tregs using Foxp3DTR mice revealed that Tregs suppress the abundance of MHCII+CAFs in tumors by inhibiting CD4 T cell responses that can directly control primary tumor growth and metastatic progression. Functionally, MHCII expression on fibroblasts was required for CD4 T cell control of PDAC progression upon Treg ablation. Collectively, our findings identify an IFN{gamma}-driven, antitumor activity of MHCII expression on CAFs and reveal that CAFs may be harnessed to promote adaptive immunity to PDAC.

papers.title: Polygenic polymorphisms cooperate to drive expansion of HCMV adaptive NK cell and NK-like T cell populations
papers.abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) infection drives the expansion of several innate and innate-like lymphocyte populations. Characterized by high cell surface expression of NKG2C, these populations include the adaptive CD56+ Fc{epsilon}RI{gamma}- NK cell, an NK-like TCR{beta}+CD8+ T cell population and a V{gamma}9/V{delta}1+ T cells. Beyond NKG2C expression, both the adaptive NK cell and the NK-like T cell population exhibit enhanced cytokine response to antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC). Expansion of each population is only observed in 30-40% of HCMV+ individuals and is independent of expansion of each other. In this study, we evaluated 200 healthy donors and identified several immunogenetic factors that influence NKG2C expression across the three lymphocyte populations. NKG2C (KLRC2) copy number and allelic polymorphism was associated with NKG2C+ NK cell frequency and surface expression density in HCMV- but not in HCMV+ individuals. Investigating other genetic loci encoding proteins related to adaptive NK function, we found that CD16a and HLA-E alleles act cumulatively with NKG2C copy number to drive NKG2C expression on lymphocytes among HCMV+ individuals. Polymorphism of the NKG2C ligand HLA-E influences strength of NK cell activation via NKG2C, where NK responsiveness was lower in individuals with the HLA-E*01:03 genotype, while CD16a polymorphism influenced strength of ADCC response among NKG2C+ TCR{beta}+CD8+ T cells. Based on these observations, we conclude that genetic polymorphisms in NKG2C, CD16a and HLA-E shape the NKG2C+ repertoire, influence NKG2C-mediated NK function and dictate capacity of ADCC in response to HCMV infection. Immunogenetic polymorphism among NKG2C-related genes therefore tunes innate immunity to HCMV infection providing additional protection beyond adaptive immunity.

papers.title: IL-23 licenses the transition from preclinical autoimmunity to inflammatory arthritis through IL-17A-dependent mechanisms
papers.abstract: Objectives: The mechanisms driving transition from systemic autoimmunity to clinical rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remain poorly understood. We investigated the role of interleukin-23 (IL-23) in disease transition using a murine model of experimental arthritis, complemented by human transcriptomic analyses in individuals at risk of RA and RA synovial tissue. Methods: Collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) was induced in less susceptible C57BL/6 mice and combined with sustained systemic IL-23 overexpression. Disease severity, histopathology, immune responses, and tissue gene expression were evaluated. The contribution of IL-17A was assessed using a neutralizing anti-IL-17A antibody. Expression of IL-23 pathway-related genes was assessed in whole-blood transcriptomic data from a large cohort of first-degree relatives of patients with RA (n=1080) and in an independent synovial RNA-sequencing dataset (n=218). Results: In mice, sustained IL-23 overexpression converted a mild CIA phenotype into a highly penetrant arthritis characterized by increased expression of innate inflammatory mediators, and enhanced antigen-specific production of IL-17A and IFN-{gamma}, despite unchanged collagen-specific antibody responses. Neutralization of IL-17A prevented arthritis development. In human whole blood longitudinal analyses, lower RORC and KLRB1 expression was associated with a higher risk of RA onset. KLRB1 expression was persistently lower in progressors, whereas RORC expression showed a steeper decline before diagnosis, although this difference did not remain significant after correction for multiple testing. In RA synovium, IL23R, IL23A, and CCR2 expression was increased compared with controls, while IL23R expression was higher in early than established RA. Conclusions: IL-23 acts as a critical regulator of the transition from systemic autoimmunity to inflammatory arthritis by promoting IL-17A-dependent cellular and myeloid inflammatory pathways. The change in IL-23 pathway signatures in at-risk individuals and early RA supports the translational relevance of this pathway during disease initiation.

papers.title: A biomimetic SPARC platform coupling adaptor recruitment and BRS-Lck condensation for enhanced NK/T cell combination therapy
papers.abstract: Immune cell engineering has proven to be a promising therapeutic strategy for cancers and autoimmune diseases. Compared to classical CAR therapies, engineered T cells with modified TCRs (such as STAR-T and TRuC-T) exhibit lower tonic signaling and higher persistence. Inspired by this, we developed novel Synthetic Parallel Antigen Receptor Complexes (SPARC) based on the NK cell receptor 1 (NCR1) and the TCR chain. These SPARCs can recognize target cells via engineered extracellular domains and transduce signals by recruiting endogenous adaptor proteins (CD3{zeta}/FcR{gamma}). In NK cells,SPARCs confer high antigen specificity against lymphoma and enables NK cells to specifically recognize and kill tumor cells. Mechanistically, the cytoplasmic domain of NCR1 forms condensates with Lck kinase through two conserved basic-rich sequences (BRS), thereby promoting receptor clustering and enhancing NK cell cytotoxicity. Our findings indicate that SPARCs can also be applied to other immune cells expressing CD3{zeta} and FcR{gamma}. Incorporation of costimulatory domains further improves the performance of SPARCs. Furthermore, combining SPARC-engineered T cells and NK cells showed superior efficacy compared to either cell type alone. This biomimetic design preserves low basal signaling, overcomes the recognition limitations of endogenous receptors, and provides a versatile platform for engineering other membrane complexes.

papers.title: Arginine activates a conserved sphingolipid defense axis against infection
papers.abstract: Metabolism is generally viewed as supporting immune responses rather than acting as a direct mediator of host defense. Here, we show that arginine directly activates the sphingolipid metabolic pathway in Plutella xylostella, promoting ceramide accumulation and consequently exerting antibacterial effects. Furthermore, we find that arginine synthesized by the host gut bacteria can activate this pathway, revealing an independent metabolic defense mechanism driven by gut bacterial arginine, which operates independently of classical immune cascades. Cross species validation shows that the ceramide biosynthesis pathway is highly conserved across eukaryotes, and its antipathogen effects display potential universality across insect species. This study opens new directions in gut innate immunity research, provides novel targets for the development of antimicrobial agents against insect pests, offers important reference value for eukaryotic pathology studies, and provides new insights into the development of novel therapeutic strategies against drug resistant bacterial infections.

papers.title: Proteome-Wide Serology Identifies Secreted IgD against RSV Fusion Glycoprotein as a Signature of Broadly Elevated Antibody Response
papers.abstract: Serological evaluation of antibody response using conventional indirect immunoassays cannot capture the full depth, diversity, and functional complexity of human polyclonal antibodies. Here, we developed mass spectrometry-based Proteome-Wide Serology (ProWiSe) assays for the identification and absolute quantification of antigen-specific human antibodies across isotypes, subclasses, and variable-region repertoires. Using ProWiSe, we measured the depth and diversity of serum antibodies to multiple antigens of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a pathogen associated with repeated reinfections and skewed immune response. IgG1 antibodies targeting the fusion glycoprotein F (RSVF) dominated the antibody response, with a background-corrected median level of 1,700 ng/mL across 214 healthy maternal serum samples from the general population. ProWiSe identified reproducible co-enrichment of complement component 1q complexes, revealed the usage of several dozen IGHV variable-region germline genes in the anti-RSVF polyclonal response, and suggested limited IGHV repertoire diversity in some individuals. In addition to IgG1, we discovered a complex antibody response characterized by significantly elevated levels of nearly all human immunoglobulin isotypes and subclasses, including previously unexplored IgG4 and IgD. The identification of high-affinity IgD against prefusion and postfusion RSVF, but not against other antigens studied, was the most unexpected observation, occurring in 52% of the healthy maternal serum samples. ProWiSe unambiguously identified the secreted IgD isoform P01880-1 and supported the IgD paradox of preferential {lambda} light-chain usage in secreted IgD. Detectable anti-RSVF IgD levels ([≥]0.11 ng/mL) correlated with broadly elevated antibody responses across all other isotypes and subclasses, except IgE. ProWiSe assays offer a versatile platform for quantitative serological diagnostics, exploration of depth, diversity, and dynamics of polyclonal antibody response, and discovery of rare antibody isotypes.

papers.title: Prediction of early Toxoplasma gondii infection during pregnancy combining host biomarkers and machine learning
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii is a major cause of reproductive failure and severe gestational complications in both humans and small ruminants and early diagnosis is essential to prevent adverse outcomes. In sheep, congenital toxoplasmosis can trigger early fetal death (EFD) during the acute phase of the infection (days 7-14 post-infection) when conventional diagnosis methods are ineffective. Therefore, this study aimed to identify early infection biomarkers using a machine learning approach to support EFD diagnosis and providing a translational foundation for early diagnostic strategies in human toxoplasmosis. For that, 27 serum biomarkers (cytokines, acute-phase proteins, oxidative stress and hemostatic parameters) were evaluated during the early stage of infection in 22 pregnant sheep experimentally challenged with T. gondii and 6 uninfected controls. To assess diagnostic specificity, models were tested using sera from animals experimentally infected with other abortifacient agents (Neospora caninum and Chlamydia abortus) and validated with samples from 19 natural abortion outbreaks. A four-biomarkers panel, encompassing CXCL9, CXCL10, IFN-{gamma}, and serum amyloid A, achieved over 74% accuracy in the specific detection of early T. gondii infection and 100% of sensitivity when studying natural infection cases. This approach might support the development of rapid diagnostic strategies, improving early intervention and disease management in livestock production systems. Its translation to human medicine could also aid in addressing current diagnostic gaps and facilitate timely interventions to prevent congenital toxoplasmosis and pregnancy loss in women.

papers.title: Deep phenomics of human PBMCs using a 31-marker spectral flow cytometry panel
papers.abstract: Functional cytokines orchestrate leukocyte-mediated innate and adaptive immune responses within the host following infection or immunization. In contrast, lymphocyte-mediated activation-induced markers (AIMs) are predominantly associated with adaptive immune responses. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) primarily function to balance the immune response by preventing excessive inflammation and maintaining self-tolerance. Currently, conventional intracellular cytokine tracking or cytokine-independent AIMs methodology is available for studying antigen-specific lymphocyte or T cell responses in humans. However, this approach faces challenges due to the difficulty in simultaneously deep immunophenotyping the key functional cytokine signatures, AIMs, and nuclear signature of FoxP3+ Tregs. Using spectral flow cytometry, we developed a 31-parameter panel to profile simultaneously major immune cell subsets (B cells, NK cells, DCs, monocytes) along with T cells, memory phenotypes, functional cytokines by tracking established Th1 markers IFN{gamma}, TNF and IL-2; Th2 markers IL-4/5/13 and the Th17 marker, IL-17, AIMs and FoxP3+ Tregs in human PBMCs in steady state as well as in mitogen stimulated conditions. For AIMs, CD69, CD134 (OX40) and CD137 (4-1BB) are included and validated. We also re-validated our panel to profile antigen specific Th1/2/17 cells or AIMs distribution after peptide stimulation. This optimized multicolor spectral flow panel allows a detailed immune profiling of functional cytokines, AIMs and FoxP3+ Tregs in the T cell compartment from human and might be useful for exploratory analysis of how these functional cytokines or AIMs or Tregs shape host immunity after infection or vaccination. Our panel is highly customizable, allowing researchers to tailor it to their specific requirements.

papers.title: A noncanonical function of Dicer fuels self-dsRNA-driven inflammation
papers.abstract: Self-derived double-stranded RNA (self-dsRNA) acts as potent triggers of autoinflammation and damage-associated molecular patterns in cancer and infection. However, the upstream processes controlling self-dsRNA homeostasis remain unclear. We uncover a non-canonical role for human Dicer in driving cell-intrinsic immunity to self-dsRNAs that arise from editing or splicing defects, epigenetic deregulation or mitochondrial stress. Dicer loss abolishes type-I interferon induction, PKR activation, and OAS-RNase L activation in response to self - but not exogenous - dsRNA in multiple cell types, including a clinically-relevant hiPSC model of neuroinflammation. Dicer interacts with G3BP1 and LGP2 to regulate self-dsRNA availability and recognition, respectively, independently of miRNAs. As immunostimulatory self-dsRNAs fail to accumulate and activate dsRNA sensors in absence of Dicer, these findings position Dicer as a central regulator of self-dsRNA sensing.

papers.title: Extracellular DDR1 targeting remodels collagen-rich tumor stroma and local immunity
papers.abstract: Collagen rich stroma can restrict immune cell access and sustain immune exclusion in solid tumors, but strategies that directly target extracellular matrix organizing receptors remain limited. Here, we develop cross reactive nanobody Fc proteins against extracellular discoidin domain receptor 1 (DDR1) and identify DDR1nb 3 Fc as a lead molecule with activity in immunocompetent mammary and pancreatic tumor models, including an orthotopic pancreatic model. Tumor control is accompanied by altered collagen architecture and remodeling of the intratumoral immune compartment rather than consistent direct tumor-cell growth inhibition. Single cell profiling with mouse level compositional and pseudobulk analyses reveals reproducible pathway level remodeling of tumor associated neutrophils, while Ly6G positive cell depletion significantly modifies the antitumor effect of DDR1nb 3 Fc. These findings identify extracellular DDR1 as an actionable regulator of collagen rich tumor stroma and support its targeting as a strategy to reshape the tumor microenvironment and promote tumor control.

papers.title: Anorectal care products cause variable inflammation and adverse barrier effects in a mucosal epithelial model
papers.abstract: Introduction: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and colorectal cancer (CRC) are rising in the United States, yet their shared mucosal environment remains underexplored. Rectal douching, a common practice among individuals engaging in receptive anal intercourse, has been epidemiologically linked to increased STI and HPV risk, but biological mechanisms are unclear. Methods: Using a human colorectal epithelial co-culture model (Caco-2/HT29-MTX-E12), we compared the effects of common douching products on cell viability, barrier integrity, and cytokine response. Results: Hyperosmolar or surfactant-containing solutions, including saline enemas, detergents, and soaps, caused rapid declines in metabolic activity and transepithelial electrical resistance, coupled with IL-6 and TNF- upregulation. In contrast, isotonic formulations maintained epithelial viability and barrier function comparable to buffered controls while reducing inflammatory signaling. Discussion: These findings provide mechanistic evidence that many consumer douching products compromise mucosal health and highlight the feasibility of harm-reduction designs for safer anal hygiene and sexual preparation.

papers.title: Serum Calprotectin as predictor of Rheumatoid Arthritis disease severity and Mortality
papers.abstract: Objective: To evaluate the clinical utility of serum calprotectin (sCAL) as a biomarker of disease activity, disease severity, cardiovascular risk, and mortality in inflammatory rheumatic diseases (IRDs). Methods: Serum calprotectin was measured in 2677 patients with IRDs, including 1472 rheumatoid arthritis (RA), 771 axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA), and 434 psoriatic arthritis (PsA) patients enrolled in the Swiss Clinical Quality Management in Rheumatic Diseases registry, as well as 248 healthy blood donors. Associations with disease activity, radiographic progression, cardiovascular biomarkers, incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and mortality were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic, Cox regression, and Kaplan-Meier models. Results: sCAL concentrations were significantly higher in RA than in axSpA, PsA, or healthy blood donors. Although diagnostic discrimination between IRDs was modest (Area under the curve (AUC): 0.56), elevated sCAL identified a subset of patients with RA characterized by higher disease activity, higher autoantibody levels, and accelerated radiographic progression, performing better than CRP for the assessment of inflammatory activity, particularly for the discrimination of active synovitis (SJC28[≥]4, AUC 0.67 vs 0.62, p=0.012), even in patients with normal CRP concentrations. Elevated sCAL was independently associated with increased all-cause mortality (HR:2.99; 95% confidence interval (95%CI):1.87-4.78), cardiovascular mortality (HR:7.49;95%CI:1.50-37.55), respiratory mortality (HR: 5.89; 95%CI:1.97-17.62), and incident MACE (HR: 2.10; 95%CI: 1.04-4.24). Furthermore, sCAL correlated with high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T and NT-proBNP concentrations, independently of lipid profile. Conclusions: Serum calprotectin is a clinically relevant biomarker in RA that reflects both disease activity and severity, independently identifying patients at increased cardiovascular risk and mortality, supporting its potential role in disease monitoring and risk stratification.
